interpretations.class_distribution: Class counts show screening skew: No_DR usually dominates. That imbalance is why we use class weights / careful metrics (not accuracy alone) when judging model quality.
interpretations.mean_brightness_by_class: Average luminance by grade reflects acquisition conditions (underexposure / overexposure). Systematic brightness shifts can mimic pathology cues, so Gaussian filtering + normalization stabilize training across clinics.
interpretations.mean_green_channel_by_class: The green channel carries most vessel/lesion contrast in fundus photos. Higher green means by severity often track hemorrhages and exudates becoming more visible — a clinically meaningful image feature for DR grading.
interpretations.mean_sharpness_by_class: Laplacian sharpness summarizes focus quality. Soft/blurry frames are harder to grade; sharpness gaps across classes warn that the model may be learning camera quality as a shortcut.
